template_params.gap: UTC date minus previous UTC date

prompt: The onboarding team wants to know how long new users wait between their activation steps. Take the users whose signup_ts, a moment in UTC, is from 1 July 2025 00:00 up to but not including 1 October 2025 00:00, and all of their activation events, whenever they happened. Put each user's events in order of event_ts; no user has two events at the same moment. An event's gap is the UTC date of its event_ts minus the UTC date of the same user's previous event, in whole days, so two events on the same UTC day have a gap of 0. A user's first event has no previous event, so leave it out. For each event_name, return three columns, in this order: event_name; n_steps, the number of events that have a previous event; and avg_gap_days, the average gap of those events, rounded to 2 decimals. Return one row for each event_name with at least one such event. Sort by event_name from A to Z.
hints: Next, write the same user's previous event time beside each event, then the gaps and the averages for each event name.
The previous event must belong to the same user and come before it in time; the first event has no previous time, so filter it out before you average.
why_this_works: LAG over each user's events in time order gives the previous event's moment, and subtracting the two UTC dates counts the calendar days between them.
